scenario: AITA for not ending my friendship with my best friend after he cheated on my sister? | Both my best friend and my sister know about my other account so this is a throwaway. I'm an 18 year old guy and I have a twin sister. I've been best friends with my best friend (we'll call him G) since kindergarten, so G and my sister have always been pretty close too. They've kind of had a "thing" going on our whole lives. For the longest time, they never officially dated for a bunch of different reasons I won't get into, but they were always really close and really into each other. A little over a year ago, when we were all 17, they finally started dating. Everything went really well for like 13 months, but then long story short, G cheated on my sister and I was the one who figured it out. He swore it wouldn't happen again and begged me not to tell my sister but I told her anyway. I was mad at him and he was mad at me so we didn't talk for a month and a half, which was honestly the weirdest month and a half of my whole life. G's practically like my brother, we've been inseparable since kindergarten, so not having him around was kinda....unbearable honestly lol After our streak of not talking to each other, G invited me on his family ski trip as a way to make amends (I've been on lots of his family's ski trips through the years). I accepted and ended up forgiving him and letting him back into my life because it was way too weird without him in it. I can tell he's genuinely sorry about what happened. He literally cried cause he felt so bad and I've only seen him cry like once before in my whole life Anyway, G and my sister broke up as soon as she found out he cheated and they're still not on speaking terms, so my sister obviously isn't happy about the whole situation. She's making me feel like shit for still being friends with G, and she doesn't seem to understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13 year friendship over her. I know G made a huge mistake, I hate him for it and I'll never 100% get over it, but I'm not gonna let it ruin my best and longest friendship. I think about it like this: if your best friend cheated on their SO and then felt like shit, would you end your friendship with them? No. So why is this any different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall (a different college in a different state than the one my sister's going to), so none of this is gonna be something that we even think about when we're living in different places Am I the asshole?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being an asshole in this situation. Let me start by understanding what's going on here. So, there's me, my best friend G, and my twin sister. G and I have been best friends since kindergarten, which is a really long time. G and my sister have always been close too, and they've had this "thing" going on for a long time. They finally started dating when we were 17, and everything was great for about a year. But then, G cheated on my sister. I found out about it and told my sister, even though G begged me not to. That made me mad at G, and he was mad at me too. We didn't talk for a month and a half, which was really weird for me because G is like my brother. After that, G invited me on his family's ski trip to make amends. I went, and I forgave him because it was too weird not having him around. He seems genuinely sorry, and he even cried, which I've only seen once before. G and my sister broke up after she found out, and they're still not speaking. My sister is making me feel bad for still being friends with G, and she doesn't understand how big of a deal it would be for us to lose our 13-year friendship over this. I think about it like this: if my best friend cheated on their SO and felt bad about it, would I end our friendship? Probably not. So why is this different just because his SO happened to be my sister? G and I are going to the same college in the fall, which is a different state from where my sister is going. So, maybe this whole situation won't even be something we think about when we're living apart. Am I the asshole here? I don't think so, but I'm not entirely sure. Let me try to break this down. First, G cheated on my sister, which is a huge betrayal. My sister is understandably hurt and angry. She wants me to cut ties with G because of what he did. But I've known G for so long, and he's like family to me. Ending that friendship would be really hard and would probably cause a lot of pain for both of us. On the other hand, my sister feels like I'm not standing up for her by still being friends with G. She might feel like I'm choosing G over her, which is a tough spot for me to be in. I want to support my sister, but I also value my friendship with G. I also think about how G has shown genuine remorse. He cried, and he tried to make amends by inviting me on the ski trip. That shows that he's sorry and wants to fix things. Maybe giving him another chance is the right thing to do, especially since we're all moving on to college and this might not even be an issue in the future. But then, there's the part where my sister is making me feel bad for still being friends with G. She doesn't understand how big of a deal it is for us to lose our friendship. I guess she sees it as G cheating on her, and she wants me to take her side. But I see it as G being my friend, and I don't want to lose that connection. I also wonder if there's a middle ground. Maybe I can still be friends with G but also support my sister. But how? It seems like my sister wants me to choose sides, and that's not easy. I don't want to hurt either of them, but it's hard to see how that's possible in this situation. Another thing to consider is the impact on all of us. If I end the friendship with G, it would probably make my sister feel better, but it would also cause a lot of pain for both G and me. Plus, G and I are going to the same college, so we'll be seeing each other regularly. It might be better to have a strained friendship than no friendship at all. But then, if I continue the friendship, my sister might feel like I'm not taking her side, which could damage our relationship too. It's a tough spot to be in, and I'm not sure what the right decision is. I also think about how friendships can survive even after big issues. People make mistakes, and sometimes they can be forgiven. G has shown that he's sorry, and maybe that's enough to move forward. But I also have to think about my own feelings and whether I can truly forgive him, or if I'm just doing it to avoid the awkwardness of not having him around. In the end, I'm not sure if I'm being an asshole or not. I just want to do what's best for everyone involved, but it's really complicated. I guess I'll have to weigh the importance of my friendship with G against my sister's feelings and see what feels right for me.
